rv.q: The playwright and director Daniella Caggiano have done a surprisingly good job of managing all the moving parts within an overall logical framework.
Like costume designer Olivia Vaughn Hern’s corsets, Hungry Women has good bones.
A femme-forward depiction of rage and truth.

Drama , Reviews , Comedy What if men suddenly disappeared from the planet? Melissa Maney’s darkly comic Hungry Women , directed by Daniella Caggiano, imaginatively explores that provocative question across two centuries, using absurdism, macabre humor, and a feminist lens to examine how women might reconstruct society—and what they might ultimat...

cn.t: Critics find this darkly comic sci-fi exploration of a world without men compelling and imaginative, praising its feminist lens, absurdist humor, and strong performances across three generations of women.
